description: Defines the canonical relationship vocabulary used by the A.R.I.A. knowledge graph, reasoning system, experience model, technical topology, user overlays, evidence model, and diagnostic routing architecture.

core_principle.statement: ARIA shall represent technical intelligence through explicit typed relationships between canonical entities. Relationship meaning shall be stable, directional where appropriate, context-aware, provenance-aware, and extensible without duplicating concepts.
rules: Every graph edge shall use a canonical relationship type.
Equivalent relationship meanings shall not be represented under competing names.
Directionality shall be explicitly defined.
Inverse relationships shall be defined where semantically valid.
Relationships may carry confidence, probability, context, provenance, temporal applicability, and experience weighting.
A relationship shall not imply causality unless its relationship type explicitly represents causality.
Physical relationships, causal relationships, evidence relationships, product relationships, procedural relationships, and experiential relationships shall remain semantically distinct.
New relationship types shall extend the vocabulary rather than alter existing meanings.

relationship_types.description: Source is a more specific type of the target concept.
Source has target as a more specific subtype.
Source is a constituent part of target.
Source contains target as a constituent part.
Manufacturer produces the target product or product family.
Product is manufactured by the target manufacturer.
Product belongs to the target product family.
Product family contains the target product.
Source is a technical variant of target.
Source has target as a technical variant.
Product, component, or system supports the target technology.
Technology is supported by the target product or system.
Source is physically connected to target.
Source physically mates with target through an intended interface.
Source component is physically installed on target.
Source has target physically installed upon it.
Source provides signal, power, data, or another defined flow to target.
Source receives a defined flow from target.
Source occurs upstream of target in the applicable topology.
Source occurs downstream of target in the applicable topology.
Source transmits the applicable signal toward target.
Source receives the applicable signal from target.
Source system, function, or configuration uses the target port.
Source port or component is used by target.
Source condition is a plausible cause of target condition within applicable context.
Source condition may result from target cause.
Source has an established causal relationship to target under the specified context.
Source is caused by target under the specified context.
Source may materially contribute to target without independently being sufficient to cause it.
Source failure mode may produce the target observable symptom.
Source symptom may be associated with target failure mode.
Source condition reduces performance or quality of target.
Source condition prevents target condition or function from occurring.
Source requires target for valid operation, execution, or applicability.
Source is required by target.
Source state, conclusion, function, or action depends materially on target.
Source and target are incompatible within the specified technical context.
Source is configured to operate according to target configuration or role.
Source and target values or states must match within applicable tolerance.
Source and target are required to differ according to applicable technical rules.
Source knowledge, procedure, value, or relationship is valid for target context.
Source concept, rule, procedure, or knowledge applies to target.
Source entity has target knowledge applicable to it.
Source hypothesis, condition, or component can be evaluated by target action.
Source action evaluates target hypothesis, condition, or component.
Source action or evidence can distinguish between target competing hypotheses.
Source evidence or finding sufficiently excludes target within the current context.
Source hypothesis or condition is excluded by target evidence or finding.
Source evidence increases support for target claim, finding, or hypothesis.
Source claim, finding, or hypothesis receives support from target evidence.
Source and target contain materially conflicting technical information.
Source information was derived from target information.
Source information was used to derive target information.
Source replaces target as the more current or authoritative applicable information.
Source has been replaced by target.
Source occurs before target.
Source occurs after target.
Source action should be completed before target action when applicable.
Source action should occur after target action when applicable.
Source conclusion, condition, or action is validated by target evidence or validation procedure.
Source evidence or procedure validates target.
Source failure mode or condition may be corrected by target action.
Source action corrects target condition when applicable.
Source user, organization, or team has recorded experience involving target.
Source condition, failure mode, or technical pattern was observed within target experience or case.
Source and target demonstrate a validated historical association without asserting deterministic causality.
Source condition has historically been resolved following target action in validated cases.
Source action or observation was performed by target user.
Source user performed target action or observation.
Source information was reported by target user.
Source user reported target information.
Source event, evidence, action, finding, or experience occurred within target case.
Source case contains target case-associated entity.
Source and target cases have a meaningful relationship that does not imply identity.
Source case represents a recurrence of target case or validated failure.
Source case has target as a recurrence.

rules: HISTORICALLY_ASSOCIATED_WITH shall not be interpreted as causal.
MAY_CAUSE represents technical plausibility or empirical causal possibility.
CONTRIBUTES_TO represents partial causal influence.
CAUSES requires sufficiently established causal support within applicable context.
Learning shall not automatically promote MAY_CAUSE to CAUSES based only on frequency.
Successful corrective action alone shall not automatically establish CAUSES.
Weights shall be metadata on relationships rather than new relationship types.
User-specific weighting shall not mutate the global relationship.
Manufacturer-specific weighting shall be represented through context constraints or scoped statistics.
Historical frequency shall remain distinguishable from deterministic technical strength.

context_constraint_contract.rule: A relationship may be globally valid, broadly applicable, or narrowly constrained without requiring duplicate relationship definitions.

rules: ARIA may traverse multiple relationship categories during one reasoning operation.
Traversal direction shall respect relationship semantics.
Transitive relationships may be recursively traversed when technically appropriate.
Symmetric relationships may be traversed in either direction.
Inverse relationships may be generated logically rather than duplicated physically when implementation permits.
Context constraints shall be evaluated during traversal.
Traversal depth alone shall not determine relevance.
Relationship authority, confidence, context match, and diagnostic value shall influence traversal ranking.

correct.context_and_weighting: Stored separately on the relationship instance.

anti_duplication_policy.rule: Semantic variation shall be represented through context and metadata rather than proliferating relationship names.

multi_axis_example.interpretation: ARIA can move horizontally through competing causes, vertically into product-specific implementation, outward into diagnostic actions, backward into evidence, and across into user-specific experience without duplicating the underlying concepts.

semantic_rules.rule: Every ARIA graph relationship shall use a canonical relationship type.
Relationship semantics shall remain stable across all engines.
Directionality shall be explicitly defined.
Causal relationships shall remain distinguishable from association.
MAY_CAUSE shall not be interpreted as CAUSES.
Historical association shall not independently establish causality.
Relationship weights shall be metadata rather than relationship names.
User-specific experience shall not mutate canonical global relationships.
Manufacturer-specific applicability shall be expressed through context rather than duplicate edge vocabularies.
Physical connectivity shall not automatically imply signal direction.
Signal direction shall remain explicit when technically relevant.
Evidence support and contradiction shall remain explicit graph relationships.
Derived information shall preserve its derivation relationship.
Supersession shall not erase historical relationships.
Actions may connect simultaneously to hypotheses, evidence expectations, prerequisites, risks, and validation requirements.
ARIA may traverse across relationship categories rather than remain within hierarchical branches.
Context constraints shall be evaluated during graph traversal.
Adding new technical domains shall normally reuse existing relationship semantics.
Relationship vocabulary shall grow deliberately rather than through uncontrolled synonyms.
ARIA's intelligence shall emerge from entities, relationships, evidence, experience, and changing state rather than directory location.
